claims.subject: us-eo-14110-2023

object.value: Direction to the Director of OSTP to establish a nucleic acid synthesis procurement screening framework within 180 days (Sec. 4.4(b)(i))

claims.statement: Section 4.4(b)(i) of Executive Order 14110 directs the Director of the Office of Science and Technology Policy, within 180 days and in consultation with named agency heads, to establish a framework encouraging providers of synthetic nucleic acid sequences to implement comprehensive, scalable and verifiable procurement screening mechanisms, including standards and recommended incentives.

time.note: Provision as the edition states it, dated by the Federal Register publication of 1 November 2023; the order is signed 30 October 2023. Executive Order 14110 was revoked by Executive Order 14148 of 20 January 2025.

claims.qualification: States what the order directs; it does not establish that the framework was produced, nor impose any duty on a provider. The order's own criteria for identifying sequences that could pose a risk, in subparagraph (A), and its direction on screening methodologies, in subparagraph (B), are not recorded. The dataset already holds this order's Sec. 3(k) definition and Sec. 4.2 reporting provisions; Sec. 4.4 was not recorded there.
claims.hazardNote: Only the policy-level direction is cited. The order's subparagraphs on identifying biological sequences that could pose a risk and on screening methodologies are technical and were excluded.

evidence.passage: shall establish a framework, incorporating, as appropriate, existing United States Government guidance, to encourage providers of synthetic nucleic acid sequences to implement comprehensive, scalable, and verifiable synthetic nucleic acid procurement screening mechanisms, including standards and recommended incentives
evidence.note: The subsection opens 'Within 180 days of the date of this order, the Director of OSTP, in consultation with' a list of agency heads.

evidence.passage: To reduce the risk of misuse of synthetic nucleic acids, which could be substantially increased by AI's capabilities in this area, and improve biosecurity measures for the nucleic acid synthesis industry
evidence.note: The order's own stated reason for the subsection, which ties synthesis screening to AI. Recorded as the order's statement, not as a finding about AI capabilities.

claims.subject: us-eo-14110-2023

object.value: Direction to Commerce, through NIST, to develop screening specifications and conformity-assessment practices with industry (Sec. 4.4(b)(ii))

claims.statement: Section 4.4(b)(ii) of Executive Order 14110 directs the Secretary of Commerce, acting through the Director of NIST, within 180 days to engage with industry and stakeholders, informed by the framework of subsection 4.4(b)(i), to develop and refine for possible use by synthetic nucleic acid sequence providers specifications for procurement screening, database management practices, implementation guides and conformity-assessment practices and mechanisms.

time.note: Provision as the edition states it, dated by the Federal Register publication of 1 November 2023; signed 30 October 2023. The order was revoked on 20 January 2025.

claims.qualification: States what the order directs; it is not evidence that any specification, guide or conformity-assessment mechanism was produced or adopted. The four headings are recorded at the generality of the order's own list.

notes:
Pass 3 (`screening`), prepared 2026-10-28 in a fresh context. 45 records, all in the strand Synthesis screening, all with ids prefixed ab-scr-; 18 sources, 14 document versions (one of them the dataset's us-eo-14110-2023) and 6 candidate entities (us-hhs, us-aspr, us-ostp, igsc, us-senate, us-house-of-representatives). Records by predicate: states_provision 31, published 6, introduced 3, enacted 1, supersedes_document 1, references_commitment 1, provision_not_found 1, lists_participants 1. One record is inferred (the recorded absence of a revised OSTP framework) and states its search scope; every other record is explicit; all are resolution supported; no proposed predicate was needed; nothing extends a dataset claim, because no dataset claim covers these instruments (the dataset's Executive Order 14110 records concern its sections 3(k) and 4.2, which this pass does not touch; the TC260 training-data screening provisions in the dataset are a different subject and are not re-recorded).

What was retrieved, in order: the Federal Register API (three term searches, used for discovery only and not cited); the Federal Register print of Executive Order 14110 (the same expression and SHA-256 as the dataset source and as the `measures` draft's retrieval; this draft therefore reuses that draft's source entry `gov-eo-14110-fr` and its document entry for us-eo-14110-2023 unchanged, so the two drafts share one source and one quote budget: 149 words here, 186 in `measures`, 146 already in the dataset, against a limit of 800); the HHS notices of 2010, 2022 and 2023; the HHS ASPR synthetic nucleic acid screening hub and framework pages (found through the site's sitemap after the address in the 2023 notice 404ed); the OSTP Framework for Nucleic Acid Synthesis Screening from the Biden White House archive; the Federal Register print of Executive Order 14292; the IGSC home, resources and members pages, its Harmonized Screening Protocol v3.1 and its membership application; the GOV.UK publication page and HTML text of the UK screening guidance; and from govinfo.gov the bill texts and bill-status records of S. 2400, S. 2399, H.R. 4702 and H.R. 4704 of the 118th Congress. One secondary page (ifp.org, 'How to Secure the DNA Supply Chain', linked from the IGSC resources page) was retrieved as a discovery aid for bill numbers, named no bill, and is not a source of this draft.

The two checks are clean: `tools.mjs check` reports no problems (57 quotations matched against the cached text of their own source, with 18 explicit paraphrases alongside them in 75 evidence items; every per-source budget is within its limit, the tightest being bill-s2399is at 27 of 27 words, igsc-membership-app at 16 of 26 and bill-s2400is at 65 of 86), and `tools.mjs hazards` reports no passage in a laboratory or procedural register over all 45 records. One quotation (the 2023 HHS summary) is written with an ellipsis where Federal Register page furniture interrupts the sentence in the PDF text layer.

For the integrator: three dates are at less than day precision or are retrieval dates. The OSTP framework's provisions carry the date 2024-09 (the revision mark on the retrieved copy; the day is not stated), while its release is dated 2024-04-29 and its funding requirement's application is dated 2025-04-26 with basis effective. Four records are snapshots dated by the check date with basis listing: the two ASPR page records, the IGSC membership application (the form is undated) and the IGSC member directory listing. The member count of 45 was made by Selekoa from the page's heading-level entries; the page states no number and shows no membership categories.

The hazard-safe rule shaped what could be recorded. Every instrument read contains technical screening content, and in each case only its policy-level passages are cited: what a provider, manufacturer or funding agency must do, who is covered, which dates apply and what status an instrument has. Where a record had to refer to the category of sequences an instrument screens for, it uses the instrument's own abbreviation or a plural gloss and never its definition or criteria; four such references were reworded after the hazard screen flagged the singular defined term in the UK record.
